analysis.investment_thesis: AvenuesAI fails both Magic Formula screens: Earnings Yield of ~6.2% (EBIT 316 Cr / EV ~5,136 Cr) barely clears the floor, and ROCE of 8.65% is less than half my 20% minimum threshold. A payment processor earning 3.2% operating margins on INR 3,993 Cr revenue is a toll road with a broken toll booth — big volumes, tiny returns on capital.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 31.6% over 9 years and net profit CAGR of 43.8% — genuine growth trajectory
Near-zero leverage (Debt/Equity 0.02) with INR 331 Cr cash — fortress balance sheet protects downside
Dominant CCAvenue payment gateway brand with multi-product ecosystem (BillAvenue, ResAvenue, TrustAvenue) creates switching costs
key_risks: ROIC of ~8.65% (ROCE) is well below the 20% hurdle — capital is not being deployed productively
FCF collapsed from +428 Cr in FY24 to -304 Cr in FY25 on INR 376 Cr capex — capital intensity is rising, not shrinking
Promoter stake at only 27.29% is concerningly low for a founder-led fintech; suggests limited skin-in-the-game alignment
red_flags: Operating margin of 3.23% and gross margin of 6.62% are sub-par for any software business — these are payment processing pass-through economics, not software economics
OCF of INR 72 Cr vs. Net Profit of INR 236 Cr in FY25 = 30% FCF conversion — earnings quality is poor
CWIP surged to 311 Cr in FY24 before dropping to 140 Cr in FY25; heavy investment cycle with uncertain payoff
Name change to 'AvenuesAI' in January 2026 smells like an AI rebrand narrative rather than fundamental business transformation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT (operating income) = INR 316 Cr for FY25. Enterprise Value = Market Cap 5,294.6 + Total Debt 172 - Cash 331 = ~5,136 Cr. Earnings Yield = 316/5,136 = 6.2% — this just barely clears my 6% minimum but is nowhere near the 12%+ that signals genuine cheapness. Return on Capital (ROCE as reported) = 8.65%, less than half the 20% threshold I require. A business that earns 8.65% on capital deployed while trading at an earnings yield of 6.2% has almost zero margin of safety. Both legs of the Magic Formula are broken simultaneously.

The revenue story is legitimately impressive — 31.6% CAGR over 9 years — but the business model generates razor-thin economics. INR 3,993 Cr in revenue producing only INR 316 Cr operating income (3.23% margin) tells me this is primarily a payment volume pass-through business, not a software business commanding pricing power. The FY25 capex of INR 376 Cr produced negative free cash flow of -304 Cr; capital intensity is accelerating at exactly the moment when earnings quality is deteriorating. Until ROIC sustainably crosses 15-20% and earnings yield exceeds 10%, this stock does not belong in a Magic Formula portfolio.
